summary: Chapter 3 stages the required beats — the co-signature, Berta's flat lie, the filing of Aebischer beside Vogel — but the prose keeps stopping to spell out what a gesture, a nod, or a signature means, tripping the brief's forbidden explanatory-psychology line again and again even though the bureaucratic register and the closing aphorism still show the author underneath.

issues.unit: denn er wusste, dass dieser Augenblick über alles entscheiden würde
issues.fix_hint: Cut the causal clause naming what he knew; keep only the hand over the paper.

issues.unit: Mit dieser Unterschrift besiegelte er nicht nur den Tod Aebischers
issues.fix_hint: Delete the narrator's gloss on what the signature means; let the signing beside Feuz's double-underlined name stand alone.

issues.unit: wirkte sehr traurig und sehr müde
issues.fix_hint: Replace the two feeling-adjectives with one concrete observed detail instead of naming her emotion.

issues.unit: keine Kraft mehr besass, es infrage zu stellen
issues.fix_hint: Cut the clause explaining her resignation; let 'Es war keine Frage' stand without the reason attached.

issues.unit: dachte über alles nach, was geschehen war
issues.canon_ref: steer toward: Lakonische Feststellungen des Entsetzlichen (missing)
issues.fix_hint: Cut the vague summary of thinking; replace with one concrete action or observed detail.

issues.unit: Es war ein Nicken, das bedeutete: ich weiss es, und ich werde nichts sagen
issues.fix_hint: Cut the spelled-out translation of the nod; let 'Rutz nickte' stand undecoded.

issues.unit: er erkannte darin sein eigenes Urteil
issues.fix_hint: Cut the stated realization; leave the two file covers side by side to carry it.

issues.unit: war am Ende das Gefängnis geworden, in dem er sich
issues.fix_hint: Cut this explanatory sentence; let the locked cabinet and the closing aphorism about the files carry the meaning.
